A.rationale: The compact heading, controls and header row lead directly to the comparison at each width.
strengths: At desktop and tablet all eight rows follow a single card toolbar.
Price, throughput and warranty are easy to spot in the grid.
defects: The mobile toolbar uses three lines before the first model row.
A.opportunity: Group the mobile count and scroll cue on one line so the specifications arrive sooner.

B.rationale: Serif display type creates a clear entry point, while right-aligned numeric values and a consistent sans serif keep the table readable.
strengths: The complete Operating noise label fits on one line at 390 px.
Price and time values line up down their respective columns.
defects: Some extra-bold labels, especially the brand and model headers, look dense next to the light headline.
B.opportunity: Use a slightly lighter model weight while retaining its size advantage.

C.rationale: Muted greens and thin dividers establish clean separation with little competition for the actual measurements.
strengths: Alternating rows and vertical rules make values easy to follow across desktop columns.
Small analyzer pictograms stay beside names at tablet and disappear on mobile.
defects: At 390 px the right edge reads as a complete Birch column, so the offscreen column is visually understated.
C.opportunity: Show a narrow edge fade or other continuous cue when more columns are available.

D.rationale: The instrument glyphs, earthy palette and modest header make a coherent lab tool.
strengths: The icons add a product cue without consuming a separate image row.
The two-model tablet state keeps the same visual language.
defects: The three tiny illustrations look similar enough that model names do most of the work.
D.opportunity: Make the model icons more distinguishable at their current size or use a single shared symbol.

E.rationale: Both filter states are legible, the 390 px view names horizontal scrolling, and the browser confirms filtering and reset.
strengths: Hide Alder A2 describes the action clearly and has distinct on and off states.
The mobile reset returns three models and all eight rows in the browser evidence.
defects: Cedar starts offscreen, and the scroll cue is small and at the far right of the toolbar.
E.opportunity: Place a stronger scroll cue next to the model headers.

F.rationale: The comparison grid, labels and toolbar stay aligned through reset and filtering, with no page overflow or reported axe findings at the measured widths.
strengths: The extracted comparison text includes the caption and all source values after reset.
The compact two-model tablet state retains the same column and row logic.
defects: The small-screen reset image shows the leftmost columns only, leaving row-header persistence during horizontal scrolling unverified.
F.opportunity: Check keyboard scrolling and verify that the row headers stay in view when reaching Cedar.

visual_problems: The mobile toolbar occupies three lines.
Cedar sits just beyond what looks like a finished right edge.
The heaviest model and brand weights draw more ink than surrounding labels.
effective_decisions: Emphasis on price, throughput and warranty matches the decision.
Subtle striping and a column grid guide lateral reading.
Compact pictograms are omitted at 390 px to protect useful table space.

A.rationale: The compact page title and count lead into the data, though the illustration row competes with the specification rows.
strengths: A narrow top area leaves the full grid visible at 834 px.
The 390 px count, scroll cue and controls sit together.
defects: The analyzer art keeps a tall header even when the filtered state contains just two rows.
A.opportunity: Reduce the product image height in the comparison header, particularly in the two-row state.

B.rationale: Specifications stay legible, but the very heavy, tightly spaced display face is used in several dense locations.
strengths: Every row name including Operating noise fits at 390 px.
Column values consistently share a left alignment.
defects: The desktop title letters nearly touch, and model names, prices and warranty text all use a similarly dense face.
Left-aligned prices provide a weaker numerical edge than the right-aligned columns elsewhere in the packet.
B.opportunity: Reserve the heaviest face for branding and use clearer tabular numerals for the data.

C.rationale: The cool neutral card and teal top bar are well balanced, with subtle row striping and clear column divisions.
strengths: The product drawings use consistent scale and distinct casing colors at 834 px.
The table's borders are visible without dominating the data.
defects: At 390 px the clipping edge crosses the Birch illustration abruptly.
C.opportunity: Give the scroll edge a clearer visual transition and shorten the illustration area.

D.rationale: Instrument drawings, a signal-like brand mark and coordinated technical colors create a recognizable product family.
strengths: Three casing treatments help distinguish models.
The cool palette carries coherently through both tablet states.
defects: The oversized art and unusually heavy type push the header toward a catalog presentation.
D.opportunity: Keep distinctive illustrations but reduce their prominence against the decision data.

E.rationale: The browser confirms correct filtering and reset, with a mobile scroll cue and a conspicuous reset button.
strengths: The tablet filtered image preserves Birch and Cedar with the right price and warranty values.
All top controls remain visible together at 390 px.
defects: At 390 px a partial Birch illustration gives an overflow clue, but the dense toolbar can take a moment to parse.
The available exercise does not show reaching the final column by keyboard.
E.opportunity: Keep the compact toolbar while making the scroll container's keyboard focus and extra columns obvious.

F.rationale: The same table and controls hold together across widths and interaction states, with no page overflow reported.
strengths: Extracted mobile reset text reproduces the full source table.
The filtered layout redistributes space without losing either remaining model heading.
defects: The table capture set omits a horizontally scrolled state, and extracted text provides no direct evidence of row-header scope.
F.opportunity: Verify scoped row and column headers and capture the table scrolled to Cedar.

visual_problems: The heavy display face crowds the title, model labels and emphasized values.
The illustrated header is taller than the two data rows in the filtered view.
The mobile clipping edge cuts through the Birch illustration.
effective_decisions: The compact mobile toolbar locates actions beside the count and scroll cue.
Model drawings differentiate the equipment consistently.
Column divisions and row striping hold together after filtering.

A.rationale: The banner establishes context clearly, but the hero and stacked card header delay the data, particularly on mobile.
strengths: The standalone Specifications heading and count give the tool a clear starting point.
The filtered count explicitly identifies differing specifications.
defects: At 390 px the first numeric row starts around 590 px down the page.
At 834 px the longer filtered count moves the controls to a new row.
A.opportunity: Compress the banner at narrow widths and reserve a stable slot for count and controls at tablet width.

B.rationale: The straightforward sans serif is readable and right-aligned figures line up cleanly across model columns.
strengths: Model headings and full numeric units remain legible at tablet and desktop.
The page title scales to a clear two-line heading at 390 px.
defects: Operating noise wraps in the narrow row-header column.
Price gets stronger visual emphasis than throughput and warranty.
B.opportunity: Use a little more row-header width and give high-throughput tradeoffs clearer type emphasis.

C.rationale: The teal shell and white grid have a calm instrument-console palette, with some avoidable visual competition.
strengths: Restrained table striping separates the eight rows.
A filled teal switch distinctly marks the on state.
defects: Contour lines cross the tablet headline and subtitle area.
At 390 px the tall opening and separate reset and scroll rows stretch the upper half.
C.opportunity: Move the contour motif clear of the tablet text and compress the mobile toolbar.

D.rationale: A dark teal instrument palette, product glyphs and contour motif create a consistent topical identity.
strengths: Icons differentiate the three model headers without using large product images.
The banner motif is omitted in the narrow composition.
defects: The large marketing-style banner carries more visual weight than the comparison in the initial mobile view.
D.opportunity: Carry the identity in a smaller banner or through the table's own header.

E.rationale: Filtering and reset pass, and the narrow view gives scrolling an explicit full-width cue.
strengths: The filtered tablet image shows the correct surviving columns and rows.
Hide Alder A2 and Reset comparison have direct action labels.
defects: On mobile the hint is prominent, but all data starts after several stacked control bands.
The capture shows no right edge continuation in the initial Birch column.
E.opportunity: Bring the controls and table closer together and cue additional columns at the clipping edge.

F.rationale: The same table data and controls persist across widths and reset with no page overflow in the browser report.
strengths: A caption appears in the extracted comparison text.
The 390 px reset capture keeps the full labels and units for the visible models.
defects: Wrapping changes toolbar placement at the same tablet width after filtering.
The browser could not resolve the desktop and tablet reset button contrast automatically because of a reported overlap.
F.opportunity: Stabilize the toolbar at 834 px and verify reset contrast and mobile scroll focus.

visual_problems: The tablet contour illustration crosses behind headline text.
The first value is pushed to about 590 px on mobile.
The tablet filter state wraps the toolbar to a new line.
effective_decisions: Right-aligned prices and measurements aid comparison.
The mobile scrolling hint gets a dedicated readable band.
The filtered count explains that the remaining specifications differ.

pairs.rationale: Its smaller model glyphs and lighter data typography put price, throughput and warranty first. At 390 px both visible models and all row labels fit cleanly within the grid.

It reaches the first value roughly 190 px sooner on mobile and keeps the tablet toolbar in place when filtering. The other output has cleaner numerals, but its banner and stacked controls demand more scrolling.
The compact table and consistent toolbar prioritize the comparison across widths. Its mobile rows keep full labels on one line and its tablet heading stays clear of decorative graphics.

A.rationale: The page purpose, progress, form and primary action have an immediately clear reading order at all three widths.
strengths: At 390 px the numbered progress rail converts into an evenly spaced horizontal stepper.
The desktop success card gives the confirmation and reference their own focal area.
defects: On mobile, the invalid email message and permanent help each wrap, lengthening the form.
A.opportunity: Bring the format guidance and email help together in the error state.

B.rationale: The restrained serif page title and quieter sans-serif form create a useful division between page context and interaction.
strengths: The desktop and mobile titles remain clear at their different scales.
Required text is close to each field label, and the reference code has a distinct, readable treatment.
defects: At 390 px the smallest step labels carry much of the progress information.
B.opportunity: Give the mobile inactive step labels a little more size or weight.

C.rationale: Pale olive, dark green and white keep attention on the work, with a clear red validation accent.
strengths: The progress rail and form footer meet cleanly at desktop and tablet.
The mobile Continue button spans the form, balancing the single-column inputs.
defects: The double red outline around the invalid mobile field is visually heavy.
C.opportunity: Clarify focus and validation with a lighter, visibly distinct pair of treatments.

D.rationale: Warm neutrals, a small schematic and facilities typography form a measured identity.
strengths: The diagram has low visual contrast and does not get in the way of progress.
The green button, progress marker and success accent form a consistent palette.
defects: The success page swaps the progress layout for a generic centered card, losing part of the flow's visual context.
D.opportunity: Retain a small completion cue that relates back to the numbered progress pattern.

E.rationale: The required labels, full-width mobile action and inline correction make the first step easy to use, and the supplied workflow reaches success.
strengths: The bad email remains editable with a visible format example, populated site name and the first step active.
The browser verifies the desktop return to site details, preserved data in review, and FM-2047.
defects: Email guidance competes with the immediately adjacent correction when validation is active.
The success capture confirms submission without identifying Harbor Annex.
E.opportunity: Repeat the submitted site in the confirmation to disambiguate the request.

F.rationale: The form, responsive stepper and outcome use consistent card and input styling, with no horizontal overflow at all three measured widths.
strengths: The flow report confirms that all four review values survive the tested Back sequence.
The invalid field expands the card and leaves Continue visible.
defects: Automated contrast checking could not resolve the step numbers because of a pseudo-element background, or the 390 px Review label.
F.opportunity: Verify focus order, step-label contrast and announcement of field errors and success.

visual_problems: The mobile email help and validation text both wrap below the same input.
The focused red email outline has a heavy double edge.
The final card removes the earlier progress treatment.
effective_decisions: Inline required labels stay close to the labels they qualify.
The mobile Continue button is full width.
The narrow validation message provides a concrete email format.

A.rationale: The navy progress area and white form create a strong split, with a short mobile path from progress to fields.
strengths: At 390 px the first action comes soon after the two inputs.
The desktop success state keeps the steps and puts the outcome and reference in the form area.
defects: A sizeable blank area remains below Continue at desktop and tablet.
The Site details instruction largely restates the labels directly below it.
A.opportunity: Tighten the desktop and tablet panel height around the active content.

B.rationale: Large headings are clear, but the very heavy face recurs in small controls and competes with more useful content.
strengths: The field entry type is open and easy to read at 390 px.
The placeholder formats and dark form text are distinct in the mobile state.
defects: Heavy progress labels and the compact reference lettering look dense.
The small Required labels sit far across desktop fields from their names.
B.opportunity: Use one step lighter for small labels and place Required next to the field names.

C.rationale: The navy and lime palette separates progress from the form clearly, though the two-panel composition is visually weighted to the left.
strengths: The lime active step and completion check make state easy to pick out.
The background grid remains contained in the desktop and tablet progress panel.
defects: On desktop and tablet the large navy sidebar and shadow do more visual work than the two-field form needs.
The email error frame mixes blue and red rings in a tight space.
C.opportunity: Reduce the panel's minimum height and refine the focused invalid state.

D.rationale: The navy panel, lime mark and lightly drawn schematic feel specific to a facilities service and survive the mobile reflow.
strengths: Brand mark and step accents use the same distinctive color pairing.
The desktop success page retains the same progress shell and marks each step complete.
defects: The top-right Facilities services label adds a secondary focus to the already complete brand and request header.
D.opportunity: Let the wordmark and request title carry the mobile header.

E.rationale: Mobile validation leaves the invalid field and Continue visible, and the browser confirms return, review and submission.
strengths: The email error adds a text line and icon directly under the field.
The original site is named in the final success panel.
defects: The validation message says to enter a valid email without repeating the format hint that disappeared when the invalid value was typed.
At wider widths the Required tags are physically separated from their labels.
E.opportunity: Include an email example in the visible error message.

F.rationale: The shared request frame adapts from a sidebar to a top panel and remains intact after submission without reported page overflow.
strengths: The browser successfully selects the native HVAC option and verifies all four review values after Back.
The mobile error adds space under the field without moving the progress or labels out of view.
defects: The report leaves the decorative Continue arrow's contrast check incomplete, and the transition focus behavior was not exercised.
F.opportunity: Check the keyboard path through validation, step changes and success.

visual_problems: The large navy panel and card height leave excess space on desktop and tablet.
Required sits on the far edge of each input label row.
Small bold text and the double blue-red email outline are visually dense.
effective_decisions: Mobile progress and fields fit in a compact card.
Lime clearly identifies current and completed states.
The success card preserves progress and repeats the submitted site.

A.rationale: The form has a clear sequence from overall request through progress, active step, inputs and Continue.
strengths: The active step has both a highlight in the rail and an explicit Step 1 of 3 label in the form.
At 390 px the validation message and primary action fit in the same visible card.
defects: Step 1 of 3 repeats the immediately preceding mobile progress signal.
The desktop confirmation has considerable empty space below the reference.
A.opportunity: Remove the duplicate progress cue at narrow widths if the accessible equivalent remains clear.

B.rationale: The serif headings make page and section levels distinct, with clear entered values in a quieter body face.
strengths: At tablet width the step title scales down and labels remain aligned to the inputs.
The reference is visually separated with a compact, code-like type treatment.
defects: The small labels, error copy and Continue use an especially heavy face.
The heading and the section title are close in visual treatment on mobile.
B.opportunity: Lighten small functional text and keep the top heading visually dominant.

C.rationale: Soft greens and cream separate the progress and form zones while retaining a clear action color.
strengths: The current step has both an active number and a tinted background.
The floor plan stays behind quiet space at desktop and is absent from the narrow progress bar.
defects: The red outline around the focused mobile email field comes close to the label above it.
C.opportunity: Add a little vertical room for the email focus outline.

D.rationale: The floor-plan schematic, colored progress rail and typography make an understated, recognizable Fieldmark identity.
strengths: The same shell and three checkmarks make the successful outcome feel continuous.
The illustration evokes site work without occupying the form area.
defects: At 390 px Facilities operations competes slightly with the wordmark.
D.opportunity: Keep the brand mark and move or suppress the ancillary descriptor in the narrow header.

E.rationale: The prominent current step, direct required labels and format example support correction, with a successful tested return and submission.
strengths: The invalid-email capture keeps Harbor Annex, shows the correction directly below the field and leaves Continue visible.
Confirmation names Harbor Annex and makes FM-2047 easy to pick out.
defects: The narrow Continue button remains right-aligned with less tap width than the form.
Keyboard progression and success announcement remain to be confirmed.
E.opportunity: Use the available mobile width for the primary action.

F.rationale: The panel and progress component keep their structure from initial entry through success and reflow cleanly at all three widths.
strengths: The browser checks the HVAC native select, persistence across the tested Back sequence and all four review values.
The form's invalid state expands within the existing card without clipping.
defects: The supplied automation leaves the decorative arrow contrast incomplete and does not exercise review-to-edit focus or missing-system validation.
F.opportunity: Verify keyboard focus and announcements across transitions, including the unselected property system.

visual_problems: The narrow view repeats the current step in the rail and heading area.
Small labels, error copy and the primary action are very heavy.
The desktop confirmation leaves a large blank area below the reference.
effective_decisions: The current step combines number, label and background.
The mobile error shows an immediately usable correction example.
The success state completes the stepper, names the site and highlights the reference.

pairs.rationale: Its compact mobile stepper and error treatment keep the action close, and completed progress plus the site name improve confirmation. The other entry has lighter small text and a wider mobile action.

Its labels, required markers and email guidance are easier to scan as one unit, while the short, quieter desktop card better fits a two-field step. The navy entry has stronger confirmation continuity and more compact initial mobile content.

It uses a smaller desktop area, puts required information alongside the inputs and supplies an example in the actual error. Both preserve completed progress and identify the submitted site on success.
